title: Data Comparison with Sets
instructions: Use set operations to combine and compare groups of data. These are like mathematical operations on sets!
steps: Task 1: Combine `set_a` and `set_b` using **union** (`|`) - all elements from either set
Task 2: Find common elements between `set_a` and `set_c` using **intersection** (`&`)
Task 3: Find premium users who are NOT active subscribers using **difference** (`-`)
Task 4: Find elements in either `set_c` OR `set_b` but NOT both using **symmetric difference** (`^`)
solution:
combined_unique_numbers = set_a | set_b
common_elements = set_a & set_c
stale_premium_users = premium_users - active_subscribers
unique_to_each_set = set_c ^ set_b
hints: Task 1: Union (`|`): All elements from both sets. Example: `set_a | set_b`
Task 2: Intersection (`&`): Elements that are in BOTH sets. Example: `set_a & set_c`
Task 3: Difference (`-`): Elements in first set but NOT in second. Example: `premium_users - active_subscribers`
Task 4: Symmetric difference (`^`): Elements in either set but NOT in both. Example: `set_c ^ set_b`
Remember: Order matters for difference! `A - B` ≠ `B - A`
These operations create NEW sets - original sets remain unchanged

tests.name: Check set operations
